records.name: Our Lady of Mount Carmel Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish at 3rd and Wolf Streets in South Philadelphia with Sunday Masses at 8 and 10:30 am, weekday morning Mass, and a children's faith program (PREP/CCD) for grades 2 to 8.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass, or register a child for PREP/CCD faith classes. The parish office also helps with baptism, marriage preparation, and home communion visits for people who are sick or homebound.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 8 and 10:30 am. Saturday Mass at 4 pm, with confession 3:15 to 3:45 pm. Weekday Mass at 7:30 am, and at 6:30 and 7:30 am on holy days.

locations.label: Church (SE corner of 3rd and Wolf Sts.)

cost.text: Mass is free to attend. PREP/CCD classes for children have a registration fee, $200 for the 2026 to 2027 year.

first_step.how: Come to a Sunday Mass at 8 or 10:30 am, or call the Parish Office at 215-334-7766 if you are new to the parish.
first_step.basis: Mass is open to anyone, and the site asks new or relocating residents to call the parish office, so the way in is clear.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone, and the site does not describe what happens during the service. Children join PREP/CCD classes for grades 2 to 8 through a yearly registration, and the 2026 to 2027 registration closed on August 31, 2026.
first_visit_tips: Saturday Mass is at 4 pm, and Sunday Masses are at 8 and 10:30 am.
The Parish Office is open Monday to Friday, 9 am to noon, at 215-334-7766.
PREP/CCD registration needs the form, the required church documents, and the fee. Call the PREP office at 215-789-0849 with questions.

records.notes: Tier 1 said Saturday confession ran 3:15 to 4 pm; the parish facts page says 3:15 to 3:45 pm, which is used here. The PREP/CCD overview page says it was last updated June 18, 2024, so the 2026 to 2027 registration page is treated as the current one. Registration ran April 12 to August 31, 2026. The overview page says classes usually meet Tuesdays or Wednesdays, 4:15 to 5:15 pm, and may change. The site does not mention wheelchair access, parking, transit, or languages other than English, so access is left out. The site lists the pastor's email olmc-phila@verizon.net and the PREP office email olmcprep@comcast.net; the parish office email is recorded as the contact email. Status moved to active on the April 2026 registration notice.

records.name: Our Market Project
records.summary: A public art and oral history project for the South 9th Street Curb Market. It records stories from vendors, workers and neighbors, and offers public art and market tours.
records.what_you_do: Take a walking tour of the market with a community guide, read the market stories, or ask about helping with the social media work.

schedule.text: Walking tours run from June through the fall. Events are listed on the group's Events page.

locations.label: South 9th Street Curb Market (tours start at 9th and Christian)
locations.address: South 9th Street, from Christian to Federal Streets

cost.text: Tours are sold as tickets through Beyond the Bell Tours. The price is not shown on the group's site or on the booking page.

access.notes: Sidewalk ramps run along 9th Street, and the route has a managed street crossing at Washington Avenue. Some storefront entrances have steps.

first_step.how: Book a tour from the Book Your Tour button on the group's tours page. Bookings run through Beyond the Bell Tours.
first_step.basis: Tours are open to the public with a clear booking button, though the price is not shown on the page.
first_step.what_to_expect: The group's tour page says a tour takes two hours and covers less than a mile on South 9th Street, led by a local community guide. The booking page lists 90 minutes, so check the length when you book. You hear the market's history and stories, use a free digital tour app with old photos, and see murals, updated produce stands, and light boxes.
first_visit_tips: Tours are offered in English, Spanish, and Vietnamese.
The route starts at 9th and Christian Streets and ends at 9th and Federal Streets.
Some storefront entrances have steps, so ask about the route before you book if you need step-free access.

records.notes: The group's tour page says two hours and the booking operator's page says 90 minutes; both are kept in what_to_expect. The tour guide application on the opportunities page had a February 27, 2026 deadline, which has passed; the social media helper role had no deadline. The 2026 year on the September event comes from the 2026 Events heading, since the date line has no year. The news page has no 2026 dates and its newest dated item is from 2025, so it did not change the status. Beyond the Bell Tours is a commercial tour company, so it is not recorded as a group. No price is shown anywhere, so cost.level is paid because tours are sold as tickets.

records.name: Overbrook Presbyterian Church
records.summary: A Presbyterian church on City Avenue with Sunday worship, Sunday School and youth groups, choirs, and service projects such as the Kensington Project service day.
records.what_you_do: Join Sunday worship at 10:30 am, Sunday School for children and youth (September to May), the monthly youth group, a choir or handbell rehearsal, or a service day such as the Kensington Project. Newcomers can attend worship or call the office.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 10:30 am, held in the Fellowship Hall during the sanctuary restoration. Sunday School runs September to May. Weekly groups meet Monday to Thursday, and the youth group meets the first Friday of each month at 5:30 pm.

locations.label: Church building (worship in the Fellowship Hall during restoration)

cost.text: No fee is listed for worship or the groups. Giving is invited.

access.notes: The entire first floor is wheelchair accessible, and a ramp leads to the main entrance.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 10:30 am at 6376 City Avenue. To ask about a group, email office@overbrookpresb.org or call 215-877-2744.
first_step.basis: The site says visitors are always welcome, tells newcomers to attend worship or call the office, and lists each weekly group with its time.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday worship starts at 10:30 am in the Fellowship Hall, where the church meets while the sanctuary is restored after a January 2024 fire. Fellowship Hour follows the service, and you can also watch online. Nursery care for infants and toddlers runs during Sunday worship, and Sunday School takes children and youth from September to May.
first_visit_tips: A lot beside the church holds about 80 cars, and there is some street parking on Lancaster Avenue.
The first floor is wheelchair accessible, and a ramp leads to the main entrance.
Volunteers who work with children or youth go through background screening.
Call 215-877-2744 or email office@overbrookpresb.org with questions.

records.notes: The church site expects the sanctuary restoration to finish at Christmas 2026, so the Fellowship Hall setting may change. Most October 2026 event dates on the site have no year written with them, so the September 2026 newsletter is the dated evidence used for status. Several recurring groups (drama, online prayer, centering prayer, Bible study) list times but no sign-up or cost. The choir and handbell rehearsal times are listed, but the separate choir page was not read, so audition and dues are unknown. No ASL or other-language information was found.

records.name: Oxford Circle Christian Community Development Association
records.summary: A faith-based nonprofit in the Oxford Circle neighborhood. It runs an after-school program at Carnell Elementary, adult English and job training classes, family resource centers at two schools, and a regular food distribution.
records.what_you_do: Get free food on a distribution Thursday, enroll a child in the after-school program, take an adult English or job training class, or ask about the family resource centers.

schedule.text: The after-school program runs Monday to Friday, 3:30 to 6 pm, during the school year. Adult English classes run each semester: beginners meet Monday and Wednesday mornings, and intermediate students meet Tuesday and Thursday evenings. Food distribution is on Thursdays, except the second Thursday of the month.

locations.label: Oxford Circle CCDA office and food distribution site
Carnell Family Resource Center, at Laura H. Carnell Elementary School
Fels Oasis, at Samuel Fels High School

cost.text: Food distribution is free. The site does not list costs for the after-school program or the adult classes.

access.notes: The after-school registration form is also offered in Haitian Creole and Russian. The adult intake forms are in English and Spanish.

first_step.how: Walk up to the food distribution at 900 E Howell St on a 1st, 3rd, or 5th Thursday, 1 to 4 pm. No registration is needed.
first_step.basis: Food needs no registration or prerequisites, and the adult English classes list a beginner level with an intake form, but the after-school program is only for Carnell students.
first_step.what_to_expect: Food is handed out as free grocery bags, about 400 households a week. The site says no registration or prerequisites are required for food. For adult classes, you fill out an intake form first, and then the class meets at its set time; the site does not list costs or who qualifies.
first_visit_tips: Walk-up runs 1 to 4 pm and drive-up runs 10 am to 1:30 pm on the 1st, 3rd, and 5th Thursdays at 900 E Howell St.
On the 4th Thursday, people line up at 10 am at M&T Bank, 6500 Castor Avenue, until supplies run out.
For adult classes, use the Student Intake Form on the adult education page, in English or Spanish.
The after-school office is at (215) 400-3150, option 6, and is open Monday to Wednesday, 8:45 am to 2:45 pm.

records.notes: The volunteer page linked from the home page (occcda.org/volunteer-and-employment-opportunities/) returned a 404 and is listed under blocked. A search pointed to occcda.org/jobs/ as the current Employment and Volunteer Opportunities page, but I did not fetch it because this group reached its six-fetch limit, so volunteer roles are unverified and left out. The search summary's claims about that page were not recorded. The summer camp link on the site is from 2021, and the site says summer camp registration opens toward the end of spring 2027, so no summer dates are recorded. The adult education page lists WorkForce@occcda.org, which links to a different address (economicdevelopment@occcda.org); neither is recorded as a workforce contact. The Fels Oasis email on the family resource center page does not match the one shown in the text. The contact name Anita Lyndaker comes from the tier 1 IRS data and does not appear on any page I read; the site names Destiny Brew (after-school) and Lisa Serrano (food) instead, so verify before publishing.

records.name: Oxford Presbyterian Church
records.summary: A Presbyterian church on Stenton Avenue with Sunday worship in person and online, a weekday morning adult program called Literacy ED, and a Wednesday prayer time.
records.what_you_do: Join Sunday worship in person or online, the Wednesday prayer time, the Literacy ED adult program on Tuesday or Thursday mornings, or the Tuesday evening line dance class.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 11 am, in person and online. Literacy ED adult program on Tuesdays and Thursdays at 10 am. Line dance classes on Tuesdays, 7 to 9 pm. Wednesday prayer is listed at two different times, so call to confirm.

cost.text: No fee is listed for worship or Literacy ED. The calendar lists $8 for line dance classes.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 11 am at 8501 Stenton Avenue, or call 215-247-9487 or email oxpc19150@verizon.net to ask about the adult program.
first_step.basis: Worship is public, in person and online, and the site lists a phone, an email and a contact form, but it does not state a visitor welcome or describe the Literacy ED program.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday worship is at 11 am at the church on Stenton Avenue, and you can also join online. The site does not describe the order of worship or whether children have their own program. Literacy ED meets Tuesday and Thursday mornings at 10 am, but the site does not explain what happens there; the line dance class is for adults only.
first_visit_tips: The site does not give parking or entrance details, so ask the office before you come.
Use the contact form or call 215-247-9487 to ask about Literacy ED before your first visit.
Line dance is listed at $8 and is for adults only, on Tuesday evenings from 7 to 9 pm.
Wednesday prayer is listed at two different times, so call first.

records.notes: Literacy ED appears on the calendar (Tuesdays and Thursdays, 10 am), but no page describes it, so the literacy_tutoring tag carried over from tier 1 is unverified. Wednesday prayer is listed at noon to 1:30 pm on the calendar and at 7 pm on the home page; the conflict is not resolved here. The line dance class appears on two Tuesdays in October 2026 with a note that children are not allowed, so it is treated as weekly. The ministries page lists a prayer ministry, Christian education, and a community engagement team, none with schedules. The home page Zoom link carries a meeting passcode, so it is not recorded; the Facebook live link is a platform lead and is not recorded either. The worship page says online worship is on Facebook, while the home page lists Zoom. The calendar's October 2026 entries show the year only in the heading.

records.name: P&P Foundation
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that promotes journalism. It runs the yearly Philly News Awards, events with local newsmakers, training for reporters and editors, and a mentorship program that matches newer journalists, including students, with experienced local reporters.
records.what_you_do: Email the foundation to ask about its mentorship program if you are a student or early-career journalist. You can also watch for the yearly awards, which take entries about Philadelphia reporting, and for events with local newsmakers.

schedule.text: The Philly News Awards are given once a year. The site does not list dates for events or training sessions.

locations.label: Pen & Pencil Club building, where the foundation operates

cost.text: The site does not list fees for the mentorship program, events, or the awards. It has a donate button.

first_step.how: Email ThePandPFoundation@gmail.com to ask how the mentorship program accepts people and when the next event or awards call is.
first_step.basis: The mentorship program and events are described, but the site gives no application step, eligibility, or sign-up page, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a first visit. Events and training take place at the Pen & Pencil Club building on Latimer Street. The awards cover beat, investigative, sports, visual, and audio journalism about Philadelphia.
first_visit_tips: Ask in your email whether there is a fee, and what the mentorship program asks of people who join.
The site lists only an email address and a mailing address, not a phone number.
Mentorship pairs are described as newer journalists with experienced local reporters, so say what stage you are at in your email.

records.notes: Legal status: the About page calls the foundation an IRS-certified 501(c)(3). The public filing record shows a 501(c)(3) designation with no Form 990 data and no foundation code shown. The lead data includes a 2026 e-postcard (990-N) filing, and that form is not used by private foundations, so this record does not treat the group as a private foundation. The site footer reads 2025 and is not used as evidence. The Philly News Awards page gives a February 15, 2026 entry deadline and an April 10, 2026 ceremony, which makes the status active, but the page still uses future tense, so the site may be stale. The mentorship program appears on the home page only; the About page does not mention it. Tier 1 described the program the same way. The Pen & Pencil Club is named as the building partner and is listed as a lead. No journalism tag exists in the vocabulary, so professional_associations is the closest match. The contact name comes from the board list on the About page.

records.name: Palmer Doggie Depot
records.summary: A free, volunteer-run dog park in Fishtown. The New Kensington Community Development Corporation built it at the Shissler Recreation Center, and it asks visitors for donations to keep it open.
records.what_you_do: Visit with your dog after reading the park rules. To help, email palmerdoggiedepot@gmail.com about clean-ups, event setup, grant writing, or board committees. You can also join as a Bark Ranger supporter.

schedule.text: The site does not list the park's hours. Events are posted on Instagram.

cost.text: Free for all dogs and their owners. Donations are requested. Bark Ranger supporter memberships cost $144 a year or $12 a month.

first_step.how: Read the park rules, then visit with your dog. To volunteer, email palmerdoggiedepot@gmail.com.
first_step.basis: The park is free and open to dogs and owners who follow the rules, and the volunteer and Bark Ranger pages give a clear way to get in touch or sign up.
first_step.what_to_expect: The park is run by volunteers, with no attendant on duty, so visitors use it at their own risk. Owners must keep dogs supervised at all times, and leashes come off when you enter. Children 10 and under may not come in, and children 11 to 15 must have an adult with them.
first_visit_tips: Dogs must be licensed and vaccinated under city law. Puppies under 4 months, unneutered males, females in heat, and sick dogs are not allowed in.
Collars must stay on, and prong, choke, heavy chain link, and spike collars are banned.
Only standard tennis balls are allowed as toys, and owners must dispose of dog waste properly.
No smoking, food, or alcohol is allowed in the park.

records.notes: The site lists no park hours and no dated events; events are posted on Instagram, which I did not read. The Join Our Pack page lists tasks but no shifts, time commitment, training, or age minimum. Bark Ranger memberships are a paid supporter option, not a volunteer role. The board list on the About page names Mary Acker as president and does not name the tier 1 contact, Michael-Ann Matticoli. That name comes from IRS data and is not disproved here, so verify it before publishing. The site has no accessibility information, so access is left out. The New Kensington Community Development Corporation is named as the builder and is listed as a lead.

notes: The batch held seven groups, not six; all seven have records. Fetches: 41 of the 60 allowed, with no group past six (Overbrook, Our Market, OCCCDA, Oxford Presbyterian and Palmer each used six; Our Lady of Mount Carmel and P&P used five). Searches: 1 of 1, used on the OCCCDA volunteer question. No rate limits or blocks were hit, apart from the one 404 listed under blocked. Beyond the Bell Tours, the booking operator for the Our Market tours, was checked and dropped: its site describes a commercial tour company, not a community group. Partners named on the sites whose website links were not on the pages I read are in leads_only, and I did not search for them. The Our Market tour length conflict (two hours on the group's site, 90 minutes on the booking page) is kept in what_to_expect. Several records carry tier 1 contact names that the sites do not show (OCCCDA and Palmer); these are flagged in each record's notes for verification.
